messages:
John (AcmeCorp): Hey team, hitting a bunch of 502/504s right now to the hosted API when we send batch inference requests (large payloads). Started ~15:20 UTC. Our clients see timeouts and retries. X-Request-ID: rq_6f3a2c, example: https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
Olivia (support): Sorry about that — can you paste a sample request id and timestamp? any chance you have the raw curl/headers?
John (AcmeCorp): here's one full request header we logged (sanitized):
```
POST /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.example
Authorization: Bearer XXXX
Content-Type: application/json
X-Request-ID: rq_6f3a2c
Content-Length: 24567
```
And server returned HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway. No response body.
Olivia (support): thx. tagging SRE: @Raj can you take a look at ingress/edge for 502 spike?
Raj (sre): looking now, grabbing envoys in the region (us-east-1). ingress-monitor-bot: high 502 rate detected on frontdoor-lb-us-east at 15:19:47 UTC (+350% 5xx in 5m).
deploy-bot: INFO: deploy/edge-proxy v2.18.0 rolled out to us-east at 15:05 UTC by maria.
Raj (sre): hmm deploy was earlier but the spike started 15:19. Checking envoy stats and upstreams. Can you reproduce with a single large payload? Olivia, John — any throttles or sudden traffic pattern changes?
John (AcmeCorp): traffic stable, we sent a single batch job with 100 items that might have kept a long-lived connection.
Raj (sre): collecting logs: `kubectl logs -l app=edge-proxy -n infra --since=20m | grep rq_6f3a2c` — found connection reset by peer in envoy: `upstream_reset_before_response`. Also seeing `HTTP/2 stream closed` and `connection close` from upstreams.
Maria (eng-runtime): Possible connection pool exhaustion between envoy and model-workers. Any signs of long tail latencies on workers? Raj, can you pull `/stats` from envoy: `curl -s http://edge-proxy-admin:9901/stats | grep upstream_cx_`
Raj (sre): paste: `upstream_cx_active: 1023` for pool model-workers-us-east-1-s.gpu-1 (we cap at 1024). Lots of `upstream_cx_overflow` increments.
Olivia (support): overflow -> means envoy couldn't get a connection to upstream and returned 502?
Raj (sre): yes. Envoy returns 502 when it can't open an upstream connection. 504s when request timed out waiting for a response. Both present.
John (AcmeCorp): is there a short-term workaround? can you route us to a different region or model variant?
Maria (eng-runtime): quick mitigation options: 1) bump connection pool size temporarily (envoy config) 2) enable fallback routing to model-variant-lite with lower memory footprint 3) increase upstream timeouts while we triage. I'll prepare a canary change for pool size.
Raj (sre): also worth checking keepalive/tcp_reuse settings and whether workers are closing idle connections too aggressively. grabbing kernel tcp stats and worker GC logs.
Raj (sre): kernel shows many TIME_WAIT sockets and `tcp_tw_reuse` off on some nodes. Also noticing high thread switching in model-workers; GC spikes around 15:18 for a few pods.
Maria (eng-runtime): that points to worker OOM/GC pauses. Which could make connections hang and not accept new ones -> pool fills -> envoy overflows -> 502s to clients. Could be triggered by that large batch.
Olivia (support): John — while we patch, would you be OK routing to us-west? we can failover on your API key to a different region for a few minutes.
John (AcmeCorp): yes we can route to us-west for the batch. please let me know the endpoint.
Raj (sre): temporary routing: set header `X-Region-Override: us-west-1` (we have a routing cookie to honor that for debug). We'll open a quick ACL so your key can hit us-west.
Olivia (support): john, I'll DM creds/steps.
ingress-monitor-bot: ALERT: frontdoor-lb-us-east 502 rate falling after 15:30 UTC following routing change.
John (AcmeCorp): after switching, errors went away on our side. thanks.
Maria (eng-runtime): follow-up remediation plan: 1) rollout envoy pool bump `max_connections` from 1024 -> 2048 for model-workers upstream (canary 5% now), 2) adjust worker JVM/Py heap and GC flags for batch workloads, 3) add connection queueing metric and set alert on upstream_cx_overflow > 10/min, 4) add graceful backpressure on API to reject oversized batch requests with 413 when we detect likely overload.
Raj (sre): opened incident INC-2026-045: title "ingress connection pool exhaustion -> 502/504s (us-east)". Owner: Raj. Priority: P2.
Olivia (support): I've marked the customer's ticket as incident-linked and emailed them summary + workaround. John, we'll follow up with postmortem once root cause confirmed. :thumbsup:
John (AcmeCorp): appreciated. please keep me posted on the GC tuning/timelines.
Maria (eng-runtime): can take a pass on heap and batch sizing today, will post changes to #eng-runtime and link to canary IDs.
Raj (sre): immediate next steps I've taken:
- increased ephemeral pool on 2 edge nodes to drain pressure (manual override)
- spun up 10 extra model-worker replicas for us-east batch pool
- put your API key on temporary route to us-west
- added alert baseline for upstream_cx_overflow
I'll update INC ticket with logs/traces.
Olivia (support): final question for ticket: any billing impact from retries? John: our client retried ~4x — potential duplicate token consumption. We can do token refund if needed.
John (AcmeCorp): please log that, we saw ~40% spike in token counts for that window. We'll take refund.
Raj (sre): adding traces: sample envoy trace id `envoy-trace-0a1b2c`, and backend trace `worker-trace-9d8e7f`. Linking them in INC-2026-045.
Maria (eng-runtime): I'll run a postmortem draft tomorrow with GC heap profiles and envoy stats snapshots.
Olivia (support): thanks all. closing Slack thread for now, will re-open if we see recurrence. :rotating_light:
